content: MK quotes Bashir: fifteenth-century hagiography treats Qāsim-i Anvār as a man of high attainment unable to control those drawn to him; Jāmī considered some of his followers beyond the pale of Islam; a report in Aḥrār's name says followers in Transoxiana gathered beardless boys, justifying it as contemplating divine beauty, and that Qāsim asked “where have those pigs of mine gone?”; his hagiographic profile is marred and he was seen as somewhat of a failure as a Sufi master (the Rashaḥāt, by contrast, stresses his scruple for etiquette).
refers_to_primary: Bashir, Sufi Bodies, 145-46 (quoted by MK, fn 42); Jāmī; Aḥrār's hagiographer
